The three spaces

Exactly one space owns every codepoint in Base SUCS. They never overlap.

Unicode Compatibility Space

0x000000 – 0x10FFFF

Planes 0 and 1. Every value is 1:1 with the same-numeric Unicode codepoint permanently. If Unicode publishes a new version or assigns new codepoints, this space still matches — compatibility is a frozen guarantee, not a snapshot.

System Control Plane

0x110000 – 0x11FFFF

Plane 0x11. Non-printable codepoints are machine instructions that do not advance the cursor. Hosts the BANcode Registry.

Native SuperUnicode Space

0x120000 – 0x7FFFFFFF

Planes 0x12–0x7FF. The open field for OpenWindows’ own codepoints, with Traps and the Sentinel reserved at the top.

Why three?

  • Compatibility space buys interop with the entire Unicode ecosystem at zero cost — a Unicode string is a SuperUnicode string.
  • The control plane keeps diagnostics out of the text. Instructions can never be mistaken for characters.
  • The native space leaves room for OpenWindows to allocate codepoints for centuries, addressable in a single 32-bit word.

Reserved region at the top

Codepoint Purpose
0x7FFFFFF0–0x7FFFFFFE Traps — raise the instruction stream into diagnostics
0x7FFFFFFF Sentinel — end-of-stream; not an allocation

Plugins never land here: their codepoints begin strictly above 0x7FFFFFFF. See SuperUnicode Extended »
